articles.headline: Sunderland penalty against Arsenal incorrect - Premier League panel
articles.description: A penalty award strongly contested by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta at Sunderland was incorrect, according to a unanimous decision from a Premier League panel.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグの委員会、サンダーランド戦での対アーセナルのペナルティ判定は誤りと結論
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグの委員会による満場一致の決定によると、サンダーランド戦でアーセナルのミケル・アルテタ監督が強く異議を唱えたペナルティキックの判定は誤りでした。
articles.body:
A penalty award strongly contested by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta at Sunderland was incorrect, according to a unanimous decision from a Premier League panel.

Referee John Brooks penalised Gunners defender Ezri Konsa for holding Sunderland's Dan Ballard at a corner, with David Raya saving Enzo Le Fee's spot-kick as the champions ran out 2-0 winners on Sept. 12.

Arteta was furious with the decision and the club contacted Pro Ref seeking an explanation.

The Premier League's Key Match Incidents five-person panel unanimously disagreed with the on-field decision, stating: "Although it was a very untidy challenge in which Konsa initially had arms around Ballard, Ballard engages in a holding action which pulls Konsa onto him so they both fall to the floor."

The panel gave majority 3-2 backing to the decision of VAR Stuart Attwell not to intervene, however, stating it was not a clear and obvious error.

Arteta said after the match: "[The decision] is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they'd think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

"At this level with all the work we put in, this cannot happen."

The panel is comprised of three former players and coaches, one Premier League representative and one from Pro Ref.

Meanwhile, the panel unanimously agreed that Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby earlier this month should have been disallowed for offside.

Haaland's goal at Old Trafford on September 13 was allowed to stand after VAR Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus found the Norway striker was onside, but failed to send referee Michael Oliver to review the fact that Enzo Fernández was interfering with play in an offside position.

Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer Howard Webb said Donohue had "tunnel vision" over the incident, with his focus seemingly on clearing the Haaland offside and checking whether Fernandez had touched the ball.

He said Donohue's assistants, including Antrobus, should have pulled him out of that tunnel. The pair were stood down from last weekend's Premier League matches.

Pro Ref contacted United to acknowledge the error and promised a review of its processes following the incident.

In its summary published on Wednesday, the panel said: "Fernandez is in an offside position, attempts to play the ball that is close to him, and impacts the ability of the defender and the goalkeeper to play the ball in the process.

articles.headline: Evaluating surprise early-season trends for 32 NFL teams
articles.description: T.J. Watt is dominant again? The Packers can't run the ball? Drew Lock is fourth in QBR? Let's figure out which early stats and trends have staying power and which are a mirage.
articles.headlineJa: NFL全32チームのシーズン序盤における驚きのトレンドを評価
articles.descriptionJa: T・J・ワットが再び圧倒的？ パッカーズはラン攻撃ができない？ ドリュー・ロックがQBRで4位？ シーズン序盤のどのスタッツやトレンドが本物で、どれが一時的なものなのかを見極めます。
articles.body:
We're two weeks into the 2026 NFL season, which means we know everything about all 32 teams.

Just kidding.

But narratives are beginning to take hold. Which early trends will stick and which will dissipate as the season goes on? The eight remaining 2-0 teams probably won't all be playoff-bound, and the eight 0-2 teams are not all doomed. And some players have had shocking performances so far -- good and bad -- and they won't all continue.

So, what's real and what's a mirage? We tasked our 32 team reporters with identifying a trend or a stat that sticks out for every team through two weeks and sizing up whether it is likely to continue over the rest of the season.

Jump to:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

Buffalo Bills

The early surprise: Greg Rousseau is emerging as a top-tier pass rusher.

The verdict: Real. Rousseau has 4.0 sacks and nine pressures. Since 2018, the only other edge rushers to start a season with that many sacks and pressures through two games have been Aidan Hutchinson (2024), T.J. Watt (2023) and Chandler Jones (2021). That's All-Pro company, and Rousseau is doing it without fluke sacks; only one of his takedowns registers among the 20 quickest sacks from snap to tackle. His sacks appear to be products of good all-around play, not one-off big moments. -- Nick Suss

Miami Dolphins

The early surprise: The Dolphins have allowed points on 10 of their 17 defensive possessions.

The verdict: Real. Miami has yet to register a defensive stop in the first half through its first two games, and it allowed the 49ers to score touchdowns on their first five possessions in Week 2. Teams likely won't keep scoring against the Dolphins at that rate. But until first-year coach and defensive playcaller Jeff Hafley can figure out a way to manufacture a pass rush, a young Dolphins secondary will likely keep getting attacked by opposing quarterbacks. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

New England Patriots

The early surprise: Drake Maye has four interceptions on throws of 15-plus yards.

The verdict: Mirage. This matches Maye's total from all of 2025 on such throws and is the second-highest total through the first two games of a season since ESPN began tracking in 2006. Part of that is facing the Seahawks and the Steelers, two of the NFL's best defenses. Being without top wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) is a factor too. Maye's accuracy and decision-making, which are his calling cards, should improve with more time on task after not playing in the preseason. -- Mike Reiss

New York Jets

The early surprise: The defense is No. 1 in yards allowed (197 per game).

The verdict: Mirage. No doubt, the defense has improved from last season (25th), but No. 1 in the league? Let's tap the brakes. The Jets have yet to face a top-shelf offense. Ordinarily, the Packers could be in that category, but they were compromised w

articles.headline: Why 49ers' Brock Purdy looks poised for his best season yet
articles.description: Purdy is dominating through two weeks of the 2026 season despite many injuries at wide receiver. And it all started in training camp.
articles.headlineJa: 49ersのブロック・パーディがキャリア最高のシーズンを送りそうな理由
articles.descriptionJa: ワイドレシーバー陣に多くの負傷者が出ているにもかかわらず、パーディは2026年シーズンの開幕2週間で圧倒的なプレーを見せています。そして、それはすべてトレーニングキャンプから始まっていました。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Sitting comfortably on a couch in the bowels of Levi's Stadium, a question after a late August practice leaves San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy carefully considering the lessons he has learned over the past four seasons and where it might take him in 2026.

The query is simple: "Is this the best training camp you've ever had?" The response, much like his job, is more nuanced. Purdy takes a moment to ponder the offseason film sessions with quarterbacks coach Mick Lombardi and then compares where he is now to some of the highest points of his career, including the team's run to Super Bowl LVIII.

Finally, Purdy concludes that yes, he is putting the finishing touches on his best training camp. But even more than that, he knows what it could mean for the 2026 season.

"It's my fifth year and I feel confident with the plays and everything," Purdy told ESPN. "I go back and watch that Super Bowl year and it's like, 'Dude, honestly, I could have been better.' I made plays. But fundamentally as a quarterback and being consistent with my footwork, with my eyes, with throwing the ball aggressively, those were areas that I could have been better. I've honed into that."

Two weeks into the season, Purdy's words seem prescient. He has been almost perfect in blowout wins over the Los Angeles Rams and the rebuilding Miami Dolphins.

Purdy leads the NFL in Total QBR (95.0), completion rate (80.4%) and completion percentage over expectation (11.1%). He has yet to throw a ball off-target or taken any sacks. And along the way, he has posted his 13th career game with a 130-plus passer rating and eighth contest with a 140-plus passer rating -- the most such games by a player in his first five seasons.

Some of those stats are a bit deep in the weeds, but here's one that's not: Once Purdy hits 1,500 career regular-season pass attempts -- he's at 1,409 -- he will almost certainly hold the career mark for the highest passer rating by a qualified quarterback.

"He's special," said running back Christian McCaffrey on Sunday. "I think that'd be the word I'd use for it. ... I don't know what the stats are, but it's unbelievable to watch that. How decisive he is, how good he is at throwing on time and then also creating when he has to. When he's at the helm, we feel good."

Despite that year-over-year consistency, the Niners believe there's still another level Purdy can reach this season. Linebacker Fred Warner was already touting him as an MVP candidate after his Week 2 outing (DraftKings currently gives him the third-best odds at +800). And even with an already lengthy list of injuries at receiver (Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson will miss all or parts of the season), Purdy proved in 2025 that he can elevate a deficient supporting cast with his own improvement.

articles.headline: Why Aaron Glenn is encouraged by the Jets' progress
articles.description: New York is an overtime loss away from being undefeated after allowing the fewest yards through two weeks.
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・グレンがジェッツの進歩に手応えを感じている理由
articles.descriptionJa: ニューヨーク・ジェッツは開幕2週間で許したヤード数が最も少なく、オーバータイムでの敗戦がなければ無敗の勢いです。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- Perhaps the strongest endorsement for New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn came more than a year ago, delivered by his previous boss.

"If he can't [turn them around]," Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said at the 2025 NFL spring meetings in Orlando, "nobody can."

Despite a firestorm of criticism in the aftermath of the 20-17 overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers, Glenn has the Jets looking like a competitive team so far in his second season. It's overshadowed by a handful of questionable coaching decisions from the fourth quarter collapse Sunday, but he is encouraged by the progress and insisted they won't allow the crushing loss to define their season.

Glenn can prevent that from happening by beating the next opponent, which happens to be -- drum roll, please -- Campbell and the Lions. It's a delicious storyline, but Glenn, who served as Campbell's defensive coordinator from 2021 to 2024, can't let that distract him. His primary job is to re-focus his team after blowing a 10-point lead.

"It's my responsibility to get our guys to be able to close the door," Glenn said. "I take that, and it's something I will never run from."

There are some positives to build on, which should make it easier to move past the Green Bay debacle. In two games, the Jets already have run more plays with a lead (68) than they did the entire 2025 season (66). They dominated the Tennessee Titans in the opener, never trailing, and they were only one timely play away from burying the Packers.

The Jets have their best total yardage margin (+258) through two games since 1982, currently the third-best margin in the NFL. The defense, with Glenn calling the plays, is ranked No. 1 in yards allowed (197 per game). They have surrendered only 30 points, including 20 in the fourth quarter and overtime -- perhaps a troubling trend.

Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips said they will make "a conscious effort this week to step up the intensity" in the latter portion of practice, hoping there's a carryover to the game.

The Jets allowed the Packers to score on three of their last four possessions. Before that, they held Green Bay's vertical passing attack in check, though some of that could be attributed to Jordan Love's reliance on short passing because of a spate of offensive line injuries.

The takeaway-starved defense, which has gone a record 19 consecutive games without an interception, recorded its first takeaway of the season -- a fumble recovery. There could've been more, but they recovered only one of five fumbles by the Packers.

Glenn took that as a positive, saying, "We're attacking the football. We're punching the football out and I do know this: Those things are going to come around for us."

articles.headline: Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens playing with 'no egos'
articles.description: Lamb and Pickens believe their off-field connection is helping their on-field production.
articles.headlineJa: カウボーイズのシーディー・ラムとジョージ・ピケンズ、「エゴなし」でプレー
articles.descriptionJa: ラムとピケンズは、フィールド外での絆がフィールド上でのパフォーマンスに役立っていると考えています。
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- One day recently, CeeDee Lamb walked out of the locker room and into the Dallas Cowboys' weight room with George Pickens a stride behind as they laughed about something.

During training camp, most days the Cowboys' star receivers walked onto the field in Oxnard, California, together. On off days, they were often together.

About the only time, it seems, they are apart is when one lines up to Dak Prescott's right and the other is to the quarterback's left.

"I don't think you can get any much closer than we've been," Lamb said. "I feel like at the end of the day, we want what's best for each other and that's to be with one another and to grind.

"I feel like we both have that alpha mentality, that alpha dog component to us so just rubbing off on one another and just keeping this thing going. We gotta keep being who we are and at the end of the day prove it to each other every day."

Lamb and Pickens believe their off-field connection helps their on-field production. Last year, they both had more than 1,000 yards receiving, even with Lamb missing three full games and three quarters of a fourth because of injury.

Pickens set career highs in catches (93), yards (1,429) and touchdowns (nine) while Lamb joined Michael Irvin as the only receivers in Cowboys' history to post five straight 1,000-yard seasons.

The start to 2026 has been different, however, as the Cowboys (1-1) head toward Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens (1-1) in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (4:25 p.m. ET, CBS).

Lamb has caught 13 passes for 197 yards and three touchdowns. With 153 yards and two touchdowns last week against the Washington Commanders, Lamb has six career games with at least 100 yards and multiple scores, tying him with Tony Hill and Irvin for the second most in team history (Bob Hayes, 13).

Pickens has nine catches for 68 yards. He had two drops in Week 1 against the Giants, including one that could have been a 76-yard touchdown.

"I, of course, want to get him and CeeDee the ball," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I think CeeDee's playing great. I think George is playing really well. I mean, some of the catches he made [against Washington] were really big-time plays in big-time situations for us ... He just didn't have the highlight-type catches and the explosive catches and things like that. But he draws a lot of attention out there.

"Believe me, we're looking for ways to continue to get those guys the ball. And if you look at George last year, he didn't really take off until a couple games in and the rest is history."

Wide receiver is a position in the NFL known for its individuality. Some have had their own touchdown celebrations, like Dez Bryant throwing up the X or Terrell Owens, extending his arms for a "TO."

They can be moody, especially if they don't get the ball enough. Every move can be -- and has been -- scrutinized by camera angles catching poor body language, a comment or a shake of the head.

articles.headline: Rodón allows three hits in eight sharp innings as Yanks beat Rays 2-0 in doubleheader opener
articles.description: — Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings and the New York Yankees prevented the Tampa Bay Rays from clinching the AL East title with a 2-0 victory in the opener of a day-night doubleheader on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: ロドンが8回3安打の好投、ヤンキースがダブルヘッダー第1試合でレイズを2-0で下す
articles.descriptionJa: カルロス・ロドンが8回を3安打に抑える圧巻の投球を見せ、ニューヨーク・ヤンキースは火曜日の昼夜ダブルヘッダー第1試合でタンパベイ・レイズに2-0で勝利し、レイズのア・リーグ東地区優勝決定を阻止しました。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings and the New York Yankees prevented the Tampa Bay Rays from clinching the AL East title with a 2-0 victory in the opener of a day-night doubleheader on Tuesday.


              The Yankees (90-66) moved six games ahead of the Red Sox for the AL’s top wild-card spot. Tampa Bay (95-61) has a magic number of two to clinch the AL East for the fifth time in team history and first since 2021.


              Cody Bellinger hit a two-run homer in the fourth inning off Tampa Bay starter Nick Martinez (15-5) and also started a key double play to end the sixth by throwing out Victor Mesa Jr. at first.


              Rodón (7-3) struck out eight and walked none while completing eight innings for the first time since July 11, 2025, against the Cubs. The left-hander, who recorded his 100th win, became the 18th active pitcher to reach 1,500 career strikeouts when he fanned Jonny DeLuca on a slider for the second out of the eighth.


              Rodón also struck out AL MVP candidate Junior Caminero on a slider in the dirt in the seventh with a runner on after reaching 98 mph on the previous two pitches.


              Rodón threw first-pitch strikes to 15 of 25 hitters and improved to 3-1 in seven starts since returning from left elbow inflammation last month.


              Following a double by Ben Rice off Martinez in the fourth, Bellinger lifted the next pitch into the right field seats for a 2-0 lead.


              After a single by Mesa started the sixth, Richie Palacios lifted a fly ball to Bellinger. Bellinger made the catch and a strong one-hop throw to first baseman Luis García Jr. to easily complete the double play and get his eighth outfield assist this year.


              Martinez allowed two runs and five hits in six innings. The right-hander struck out seven and lost for the first time since July 9.


              David Bednar retired Yandy Díaz for his 35th save in 39 chances and finish New York’s 15th shutout in 2 hours, 2 minutes — the Yankees’ fastest game this season.


              Up next
              Tampa Bay RHP Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72 ERA) opposes New York LHP Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) in the second game.


              ------

articles.headline: Joseph Yobo backs Alex Iwobi to break Ahmed Musa's Nigeria appearance record
articles.description: Former Nigeria captain Joseph Yobo believes Alex Iwobi can push his international career beyond 130 appearances, after becoming only the fourth Super Eagles player to reach 100 caps.
articles.headlineJa: ジョセフ・ヨボ、アレックス・イウォビがアーメド・ムサの持つナイジェリア代表最多出場記録を更新すると予測
articles.descriptionJa: 元ナイジェリア代表主将のジョセフ・ヨボは、スーパー・イーグルス（ナイジェリア代表）史上4人目の100キャップに到達したアレックス・イウォビが、代表キャリアを130試合以上に伸ばすことができると信じています。
articles.body:
Former Nigeria captain Joseph Yobo believes Alex Iwobi can push his international career beyond 130 appearances, after becoming only the fourth Super Eagles player to reach 100 caps.

Iwobi reached the landmark against Portugal in June, more than a decade after making his Nigeria debut, joining Yobo, Vincent Enyeama and Ahmed Musa as the only players to make at least 100 appearances for the Nigeria national team.

Musa currently holds the appearance record at 110 but Yobo, who was Nigeria's first centurion, believes the 30-year-old Fulham midfielder has enough time and, more importantly, the commitment to add another 30 or more, barring injury.

"I wouldn't be surprised to see Alex getting to 130 or 130-plus because he's still very active," Yobo told ESPN.

"He's still performing at the highest level. You always pray and hope you don't get injured because these things can derail you.

"But knowing Alex, his professional mindset, his commitment and everything, I just hope that he goes as far as he can. Because I think the 130 barrier can be broken. Easily. Especially with a player like Alex, who is very committed."

Iwobi hit his 100th appearance in Nigeria's 2-1 friendly defeat to Portugal in Leiria on June 10, and was presented with a commemorative shirt by the NFF before kickoff.

Born in Nigeria but raised in England, the midfielder represented the Three Lions at youth level before switching allegiance to Nigeria and made his senior debut against DR Congo in October 2015.

The midfielder is poised to begin that run to 130 after being named in Eric Chelle's squad for Nigeria's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Madagascar on Friday, and Guinea-Bissau four days later, giving him an immediate opportunity to begin adding to his century.

With just four players hitting the century mark for Nigeria, Yobo explained that reaching 100 appearances starts with discipline and a commitment to sustaining the standards required to remain in the national team over a long period.

"First of all, it is your commitment to your craft, which is the skill set that you have as a professional footballer," Yobo said. "You have to act like one because in this line of career, we see people that are not so disciplined.

"It takes a disciplined player to perform well, and it takes a player who is performing well for the coaches to always pick that player. Football is very competitive. So you can't maintain the same standard and the same form for a long time without having competition."

All four centurions played over a decade for Nigeria and Yobo says that sustaining that requires a player making himself available regardless of the opponent, competition or circumstances.

The former Everton star is a good example, playing for Nigeria for more than a decade, appearing at the 2002, 2010 and 2014 FIFA World Cups and six Africa Cup of Nations tournaments.

He captained the Super Eagles to the 2013 AFCON title and became Nigeria's first player to reach the century

articles.headline: Drew Rasmussen takes no-hitter into 7th and Ks 11 as Rays clinch AL East with 6-1 win over Yankees
articles.description: — Drew Rasmussen allowed his only hit in the seventh inning and struck out 11 as the Tampa Bay Rays beat the New York Yankees 6-1 on Tuesday in the second game of a day-night doubleheader to clinch their fifth AL East title.
articles.headlineJa: ラスムッセンが7回まで無安打投球＆11奪三振、レイズがヤンキースに6-1で勝利しア・リーグ東地区優勝
articles.descriptionJa: ドリュー・ラスムッセンが7回に唯一の安打を許すも11奪三振を奪い、タンパベイ・レイズは火曜日の昼夜ダブルヘッダー第2試合でニューヨーク・ヤンキースを6-1で破り、通算5度目のア・リーグ東地区優勝を決めました。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Drew Rasmussen allowed his only hit in the seventh inning and struck out 11 as the Tampa Bay Rays beat the New York Yankees 6-1 on Tuesday in the second game of a day-night doubleheader to clinch their fifth AL East title.


              The Rays (96-61) secured home-field advantage throughout the American League playoffs and took their first division crown since 2021, when they won 100 games. Tampa Bay also earned AL East championships in the pandemic-shortened 2020 season along with 2010 and 2008, when the team had its first winning season after entering the league as an expansion franchise in 1998.


              Yandy Díaz hit two-run single off reliever John Schreiber in the seventh and had another two-run single in the ninth for his AL-leading 175th hit. Tampa Bay opened a six-game lead over the second-place Yankees (90-67) with five to play.


              In the opener, Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings as New York delayed Tampa Bay's division celebration with a 2-0 victory.


              Taylor Walls started the three-run seventh with a bunt single against Max Fried (5-5) when first base was left uncovered. Ryan Vilade hit an RBI groundout in the third after Díaz’s flyball moved runners to second and third.


              Rasmussen (16-5) was nine outs from joining Matt Garza as Tampa Bay pitchers with a no-hitter when he gave up a leadoff double to Heliot Ramos on his 97th pitch. Garza held the Detroit Tigers hitless at Tropicana Field on July 26, 2010.


              After allowing Ramos’ hit to left field, Rasmussen got the next two outs before walking Jazz Chisholm Jr. on a full count. Kevin Kelly entered and permitted rookie George Lombard Jr.’s RBI single before retiring Austin Wells on a groundout.


              Rasmussen threw a career-high 114 pitches, 72 for strikes. He threw first-pitch strikes to 17 of 24 hitters and notched his fourth career double-digit strikeout game.


              Rasmussen allowed one hit for the fourth time this year. He also yielded just one hit in six innings against the Yankees on April 12.


              Cam Booser and Bryan Baker pitched an inning apiece to finish the three-hitter.


              Fried allowed four runs and six hits in 6 2/3 innings.


              The Yankees were held to three hits or fewer for the 13th time this year.


              Up next
              Tampa Bay RHP Ian Seymour (9-7, 4.38 ERA) opposes New York RHP Gerrit Cole (9-9, 3.63) on Wednesday night.

articles.headline: Emmanuel Adebayor tips Antoine Semenyo to be the 'best and key' player for Manchester City
articles.description: Former Arsenal and Manchester City forward Emmanuel Adebayor told Antoine Semenyo to trust his ability and play without pressure, predicting the Ghana forward can establish himself as one of City's most important players.
articles.headlineJa: エマニュエル・アデバヨール氏、アントワーヌ・セメニョがマンチェスター・シティで「最高かつ主力」の選手になると太鼓判
articles.descriptionJa: 元アーセナルおよびマンチェスター・シティのFWエマニュエル・アデバヨール氏は、ガーナ代表FWアントワーヌ・セメニョに対し、自身の能力を信じてプレッシャーを感じずにプレーするようアドバイスし、シティで最も重要な選手の一人になれると予想した。
articles.body:
Former Arsenal and Manchester City forward Emmanuel Adebayor told Antoine Semenyo to trust his ability and play without pressure, predicting the Ghana forward can establish himself as one of City's most important players.

Adebayor said Semenyo has regularly sought his advice since joining City from Bournemouth in January.

"He always asks me, 'Big bro, how can I do this? How can I work on this?'" Adebayor told Ghana's 3Sports.

"I keep telling him, keep your head on your shoulders, keep working hard and believe in your quality.

"If Man City bought you, the club had 50 or 100 meetings before deciding to bring you in. You have the talent, so believe in your quality and play without pressure."

Semenyo signed a five and a half year contract with City in January after scoring 10 Premier League goals for Bournemouth in the first half of last season. The move followed earlier spells with Bristol City, Bath City, Newport County and Sunderland.

He made an immediate impact upon joining City and has remained a regular part of new coach Enzo Maresca's attack this season.

Adebayor, who joined City from Arsenal in 2009, said Semenyo has the potential to be the star of a squad already packed with established internationals.

"He's new to the Man City squad and playing alongside big players, but he will get there," Adebayor said. "At some point, he will become the best and a key player for the team."

On Saturday, Semenyo scored twice and provided an assist in City's 5-3 win over Sunderland, his first Premier League goals of the season. The 26-year-old had already contributed two assists in City's opening four league games and has started all five Premier League matches.

Adebayor's comments came as Ghana prepared for their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Ivory Coast, with the Black Stars missing several senior players.

Semenyo, Mohammed Kudus, Baba Rahman and Jordan Ayew have all withdrawn from the squad and the former City striker said those absences would leave Ghana short of the sort of experience they would normally rely on in such a high level fixture.

"Ghana have good players, but there is no game without experienced players," he said. "Kudus brings confidence to the younger players. In a derby like Ghana vs Côte d'Ivoire, you need someone to say: 'Guys, don't panic. It's 90 minutes. Stay focused, do your job and go home.'"

The former Togo captain, who currently lives in Ghana, also revealed that he played a part in persuading Auxerre defender Marvin Senaya to choose Ghana over Togo.

Senaya was eligible for both countries, and received callups in March from both Ghana and Togo, before committing to the Black Stars, with a little nudge from the former Real Madrid striker.

articles.headlineJa: 4安打の活躍を見せたグリチャック率いるホワイトソックスがロイヤルズと対戦へ
articles.descriptionJa: シカゴ・ホワイトソックス（81勝76敗、ア・リーグ中地区2位）対 カンザスシティ・ロイヤルズ（67勝90敗、ア・リーグ中地区5位）
articles.body:
Chicago White Sox (81-76, second in the AL Central) vs. Kansas City Royals (67-90, fifth in the AL Central)

Kansas City, Missouri; Wednesday, 7:40 p.m. EDT

PITCHING PROBABLES: White Sox: Bryan Hudson (5-4, 3.03 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, 59 strikeouts); Royals: Seth Lugo (7-9, 5.06 ERA, 1.46 WHIP, 131 strikeouts)

LINE: White Sox -118, Royals -103; over/under is 8 1/2 runs

BOTTOM LINE: The Chicago White Sox take on the Kansas City Royals after Randal Grichuk had four hits on Tuesday in a 14-11 win over the Royals.

Kansas City has gone 39-37 in home games and 67-90 overall. The Royals have gone 38-73 in games when they have allowed a home run.

Chicago has an 81-76 record overall and a 35-44 record in road games. White Sox hitters have a collective .404 slugging percentage to rank ninth in MLB.

The teams play Wednesday for the 12th time this season. The White Sox are ahead 8-3 in the season series.

TOP PERFORMERS: Bobby Witt Jr. has 31 doubles, a triple and 18 home runs for the Royals. Vinnie Pasquantino is 11 for 34 with two doubles and four home runs over the last 10 games.

Chase Meidroth leads the White Sox with a .271 batting average, and has 29 doubles, 16 home runs, 61 walks and 63 RBI. Grichuk is 13 for 35 with two home runs and seven RBI over the last 10 games.

LAST 10 GAMES: Royals: 2-8, .231 batting average, 5.96 ERA, outscored by 17 runs

White Sox: 6-4, .226 batting average, 4.13 ERA, outscored opponents by 10 runs
